sections.h2: What are your choices when selling a house in St. Charles, MO?
sections.html:
Homeowners in St. Charles can list with a broker, market the house themselves, or sell directly to an investor for cash. The right pick depends on how much work the house needs, how soon you must close, and whether you want strangers walking through it.

Census figures put the middle owner-occupied home value at $298,700, and 68.0% of homes are lived in by their owners. Owner-occupants make up the natural audience for a traditional listing. A cash sale tends to make sense when a house needs more repair than a retail buyer's lender will accept, when probate or a move has set a deadline, or when you would rather skip showings altogether.

  • Traditional listing: the best fit for a house in good shape in a school district buyers recognize.
  • Owner-handled sale: saves an agent's fee but puts the paperwork and the negotiating on you.
  • Cash purchase: the house is taken in its present condition and the closing date is something you negotiate.

sections.h2: What is St. Charles like, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The city is the county seat of St. Charles County and sits on the Missouri River near where it meets the Mississippi, about 20 miles northwest of downtown St. Louis. French-Canadian trader Louis Blanchette settled it around 1769 as Les Petites Cotes, and according to Wikipedia it is the third-oldest city in what is now Missouri. It served as the first state capital from 1821 to 1826, and the First Missouri State Capitol is now a state historic site.

Older blocks near Main Street and the riverfront sit in the St. Charles Historic District, with shops and restaurants on the ground floor and residences nearby. Farther out, development since the late 1970s has produced the subdivisions that make up most of the housing stock. The city is also near the eastern end of the Katy Trail, and the Christmas Traditions Festival fills the historic streets from the day after Thanksgiving until the Saturday after Christmas.

Highways make the city easy to reach: Interstate 70 and Missouri routes 370, 94 and 364. Lindenwood University sits on Kingshighway near downtown.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve St. Charles homes?
sections.html:
Most of the city lies in the City of St. Charles School District, which runs six elementary schools, two middle schools and two high schools, St. Charles High and St. Charles West. Parts of the south edge fall in the Francis Howell School District, and northern areas are served by the Orchard Farm School District.

Buyers often search by district, so find out which one covers your address before you write a listing description. Ask the district office to confirm the school assignment for your exact address.

sections.h2: What does the city of St. Charles require from a seller?
sections.html:
Under Ordinance 23-062, passed June 6, 2023 and effective September 1, 2023, sellers must provide and sign a city disclosure for every residential real estate transaction inside the city limits. A notarized copy goes to the city after closing, and the disclosure does not need to be recorded.

The form gives incoming owners formal notice of local rules. According to the city, the topics include:

  • Building and sign permits, inspections and fencing
  • RV and boat parking and storage
  • Property maintenance and solid waste collection
  • Short term rentals
  • Historic preservation districts and floodplain development
  • Site plan review, architectural review and zoning classification

Ask your title company to include the disclosure in the closing packet so it is not forgotten. Questions go to the city at 636-949-3222.

The city also requires an approved occupancy inspection for long term rentals before the first tenant moves in and between tenants. If you are selling a rental, ask Community Development at that same number whether the unit's inspection is current.

sections.h2: Can a St. Charles house operate as a short term rental?
sections.html:
Not easily. On April 15, 2025 the city amended its short term rental ordinance, lifting the old moratorium but limiting new residential permits to the Extended Historic Preservation District and lowering the cap to 0.15% of housing units, which allows up to 48 units in residential zones. The city says it is at the maximum and is not accepting new applications for residentially zoned short term rentals.

Existing permits require an annual renewal and safety inspection, a noise monitoring device, off-street parking for each rented bedroom, and a 500 foot buffer from other residential short term rentals. Commercially zoned properties inside the historic district overlay are treated differently. If a house you plan to buy or sell has operated as a short term rental, ask Community Development to confirm its permit status at 636-949-3222, and call the county at 636-949-7900 about how that use affects the property tax bill.

sections.h2: Where is a St. Charles deed recorded, and at what price?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded with the St. Charles County Recorder of Deeds at 201 N. Second Street in St. Charles. The county fee schedule effective August 28, 2026 lists $23.00 for the first page of a standard 8.5 by 11 inch document and $3.00 for each additional page, plus a $25.00 non-standard fee when a document does not meet the format rules. Card payments carry a convenience fee and personal checks are not accepted.

Your title company usually records the deed and pays the fee from closing funds. Calling the office at 636-949-7900 is useful mainly when you are recording something yourself, such as a release of an old lien.

Weather is the last thing to plan around. Wikipedia's climate summary describes humid subtropical conditions, with spring the wettest season. Check gutters, basements and the roof before inspections, particularly for houses near the river or in the floodplain, where the city's disclosure list also flags floodplain development rules.

sections.h2: What should a St. Charles seller line up before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
Get the local paperwork moving early, because the city disclosure and the county recording both sit on the closing timeline.

  • Download the city disclosure form from the Residential Real Estate Disclosure page and fill it in with your title company.
  • Decide whether the house is in the historic district, a floodplain or a residential zone, since each carries its own rules.
  • If the house has been rented, ask Community Development whether the long term rental inspection is current.
  • Confirm the school district for the address and note it in your marketing.
  • Ask the county about the effect of any short term rental history on the tax bill, at 636-949-7900.

With 30,362 households and a population that grew 2.7% from the 2020 base to 2025, St. Charles has buyers in the market, and a well-prepared file helps whichever route you choose.

faqs.q: Does the city of St. Charles require a seller disclosure?
faqs.a: Yes. Ordinance 23-062 has applied to all residential transactions inside city limits since September 1, 2023. The seller signs the form, a notarized copy goes to the city after closing, and it does not need to be recorded.

faqs.q: What is the St. Charles County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: The county fee schedule effective August 28, 2026 lists $23.00 for the first page and $3.00 for each added page, with a $25.00 non-standard document fee when it applies. Your title company typically pays this at closing.

faqs.q: Which school district is my St. Charles house in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the City of St. Charles School District. Southern edges belong to Francis Howell and northern areas to Orchard Farm, so confirm your address with the district office.

faqs.q: Can I turn my St. Charles house into an Airbnb before selling it?
faqs.a: Probably not in a residential zone. The city is at its cap of 0.15% of housing units and is not taking new applications for residentially zoned short term rentals. Call 636-949-3222 to verify zoning.

faqs.q: Do I need an occupancy inspection to sell my St. Charles home?
faqs.a: The city's inspection page ties occupancy inspections to long term rentals, which need one before the first tenant and between tenants. For an owner-occupied sale, call Community Development at 636-949-3222 to confirm.
